_comment: Cases for tools/diff_harness.py - each is fired at both the legacy Flask
backend and the FastAPI rewrite, and the status code plus the full response
body are compared field by field.
Grow this file as each domain is ported (PLAN_FASTAPI.md section 2, Phase 3).
A domain is not 'done' until its cases here are identical on both stacks.
name          required, shown in the report
form          form-encoded body (use instead of `body` for multipart/form routes)
auth          default true; set false to send no Authorization header
ignore        DeepDiff paths to skip, e.g. "root['checks']['celery']"
Volatile values (_id, createdAt, token, task_id, ...) are already replaced
with a type marker globally, so they never cause false failures.

cases.name: health: readiness
_note: Error strings are driver-specific text and the two stacks reach the same
services through different client wrappers, so the wording can differ
legitimately. The status ('ok'/'error'/'disabled') IS compared - that is
the part ArchiHUBTestRunner and the Docker healthcheck depend on.
Celery is excluded entirely because worker ping timing is racy.

_comment_next: Below: templates for the domains ported in Phase 3, in the order the plan
sequences them. Commented out via the leading underscore until the
corresponding router exists on the FastAPI side - a case fired before its
route is ported just reports a 404-vs-200 status difference and adds noise.
Remove the underscore prefix from the key name to activate one.

cases.name: types: get one by slug
cases._note: Adjust the slug to one that exists on the instance under test.

cases.name: auth: unknown user is byte-identical to wrong password
_note: Guards the account-enumeration fix: an unknown username and a wrong
password must produce identical responses. ArchiHUBTestRunner asserts
this too; do not 'fix' either side to return 404.

cases.name: lists: unknown id
cases._note: Legacy returns 200 with an array body here; the port returns 404. Expected to differ - see BACKEND_FINDINGS F13.

cases.name: forms: get one (POST, not GET)
cases._note: Retrieving a form is a POST - FormService.getForm sends POST and expects 200.

cases.name: records: favcount of an unknown record

_expected_differences: Cases that differ ON PURPOSE. Re-triaged 2026-08-10 against the running
legacy backend; each is a deliberate correction, not a regression:
lists: unknown id          legacy 200 carrying a 500-shaped body -> 404
geosystem: polygon         legacy 404 -> 400 with a reason
records: get by filters    `filepath` no longer returned (deliberate)
forms: unknown slug        same 404, different message text - see notes
auth: byte-identical      ORDER-DEPENDENT. Passes alone; in a full run the
port's login throttle (S2, which legacy lacks)
trips and the statuses diverge. Run it with
--only byte-identical, or after a Redis flush.
